prompt: Compute someone's age in whole years on a given date using java.time.Period -- the day before a birthday still counts the previous age.
explanation: Period.between(birth, on) computes the calendar difference between two LocalDates as years, months, and days, and getYears() keeps only the completed years -- exactly what "age" means. The library handles the subtle parts: the day before a birthday reports 19 years, 11 months, 30 days (so getYears() is still 19), and leap-day arithmetic follows ISO calendar rules. Hand-rolling this with year subtraction gets those edges wrong; Period is the idiomatic tool.
hints: java.time.Period.between(startDate, endDate) returns a Period object.
A Period breaks the gap into years, months, and days -- call getYears() for the completed years.
The whole method is one line; no if statements are needed for the birthday edge cases.
